## FontHeight
The height in pixels of a character of the current font, as set by [SetFont](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#setfont). Use it to place lines of text below each other.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Local small = LoadFont("Arial", 8)
Local big = LoadFont("Arial", 24)
SetFont small
Text 10, 10, "Small: " + FontWidth() + " x " + FontHeight()
SetFont big
Text 10, 40, "Big: " + FontWidth() + " x " + FontHeight()
Flip
WaitKey
```
@returns The height of a character in pixels.
@gap Fonts are the built-in 8x8 pixel bitmap font, scaled to the requested height. All characters have the same size, so FontHeight and [FontWidth](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#fontwidth) give the same number.

## FontWidth
The width in pixels of one character of the current font, as set by [SetFont](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#setfont). Every character is as wide as this value, so the width of a text is `Len(text) * FontWidth()`.
@returns The width of a character in pixels.
@gap The font is a scaled 8x8 bitmap font, so the width is the same as the height. Fonts of the original have different widths per character, and their values differ from these.

## FreeFont
Releases a font that was loaded with [LoadFont](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#loadfont). If it was the current font, the built-in font is selected again.
@param font  The font to free.
@gap A font that does not exist stops the program with an error message.

## Input
Reads a line of text that the user types, ended with Enter, and returns it without the line end. The prompt is shown first.
@param prompt  Text to show before the input. Defaults to nothing.
@returns The line that was typed.
@gap The prompt is written to the console (standard output) and the line is read from the console (standard input), even when a graphics window is open. The original shows the prompt and the typed characters on the graphics screen. For input inside a window, build a text field from [GetKey](BlitzBasic-Keyboard#getkey) as shown in that example.
@gap Without a console, for example when the program was started from a menu, the result is an empty string.

## LoadFont
Chooses a font by its name and size and returns a handle to use with [SetFont](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#setfont). The height is measured in pixels of a character, and the default is 12.

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/loadfont.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Local f
For i = 0 To 3
	f = LoadFont("Arial", 8 + i * 6)
	SetFont f
	Text 10, 10 + i * 50, "Size " + (8 + i * 6)
	FreeFont f
Next
Flip
WaitKey
```

![LoadFont](media/fonts/loadfont.png)
@param fontname   The name of the font, such as "Arial".
@param height     The height of a character in pixels. Defaults to 12.
@param bold       True for a bold font. Defaults to False.
@param italic     True for an italic font. Defaults to False.
@param underline  True for an underlined font. Defaults to False.
@returns A handle for the font. A font that does not exist still gives a valid handle.
@gap Fonts are not read from the system. Every font name gives the built-in 8x8 pixel bitmap font, scaled to the height. The name and style are remembered but do not change how the text looks.

## Locate
Moves the text cursor of [Print](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#print) and [Write](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#write) to a position in pixels. The position is on the screen and not in the current buffer.

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/locate.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
Cls
Locate 20, 20
Print "Top left"
Locate 160, 120
Print "Middle"
Locate 100, 220
Print "Bottom"
WaitKey
```

![Locate](media/fonts/locate.png)
@param x  Horizontal position of the cursor in pixels.
@param y  Vertical position of the cursor in pixels.
@gap The position is limited to the window.

## Print
Writes a line of text at the text cursor and moves the cursor to the start of the next line. When it reaches the bottom of the window the picture scrolls up. With no text it only moves the cursor. Print draws straight onto the screen, so it needs no [Flip](BlitzBasic-Display#flip). For text that is part of a frame that is drawn into the back buffer, use [Text](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#text).

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/print.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
Cls
For i = 1 To 5
	Print "Line number " + i
Next
Print
Print "Print draws on the screen"
WaitKey
```

![Print](media/fonts/print.png)
@param string  The text to write. Defaults to an empty line.
@gap Without a graphics window the text goes to the console instead.
@gap The text is drawn in the drawing color, in the current font, onto the front buffer.

## SetFont
Chooses the font that [Text](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#text), [Print](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#print), [StringWidth](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#stringwidth) and the other text commands use from now on.
@param font  A handle from [LoadFont](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#loadfont). 0 goes back to the built-in font.
@gap A font that does not exist stops the program with an error message.

## StringHeight
The height in pixels that a text has in the current font.
@param string  The text to measure.
@returns The height of the text.
@gap Text has only one line, so this is always the height of one character.

## StringWidth
The width in pixels that a text has in the current font. It helps to center text or to put things after it.

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/stringwidth.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Local msg$ = "How wide is this?"
Local w = StringWidth(msg)
Color 60, 60, 140
Rect 20, 90, w, StringHeight(msg), 1
Color 255, 255, 255
Text 20, 90, msg
Text 20, 120, "StringWidth = " + w
Flip
WaitKey
```

![StringWidth](media/fonts/stringwidth.png)
@param string  The text to measure.
@returns The width of the text.
@gap Every character has the same width, so this is the number of characters times [FontWidth](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#fontwidth).

## Text
Draws text into the current buffer with the drawing color. The position is the top left corner of the text, unless one of the two centering flags asks for the position to be the middle of the text.

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/text.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Color 255, 255, 255
Text 10, 10, "Top left corner"
Text 160, 60, "Centered sideways", 1
Text 160, 120, "Centered both ways", 1, 1
Color 255, 160, 0
Text 160, 180, "In color", 1, 1
Flip
WaitKey
```

![Text](media/fonts/text.png)
@param x         Horizontal position of the text.
@param y         Vertical position of the text.
@param text      The text to draw.
@param centre_x  1 to use x as the middle of the text instead of its left edge. Defaults to 0.
@param centre_y  1 to use y as the middle of the text instead of its top edge. Defaults to 0.
@gap The built-in 8x8 pixel bitmap font is always used, scaled to the height of the current font. Characters 128 and above show the glyphs of the bitmap font, and the text is not smoothed.

## Write
Writes text at the text cursor like [Print](BlitzBasic-Fonts-and-Text#print), but without starting a new line, so the next Write or Print continues behind it.

```blitzbasic
;media still fonts/write.png
Graphics 320, 240, 0, 2
Cls
Write "One, "
Write "two, "
Write "three"
Print "!"
Print "A new line."
WaitKey
```

![Write](media/fonts/write.png)
@param string  The text to write.
@gap Without a graphics window the text goes to the console instead.
